record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream MMLU performance across model sizes, a different measure from held-out pretraining loss, and reports results relevant to downstream scaling (V6).
record.gate_note: The report discusses scaling laws and says its data approach deviates from standard scaling laws. Figure 3 plots log MMLU error against log model size, but its plotted values are not available in the text. The reported MMLU benchmark scores below are usable results. The report does not measure held-out cross-entropy, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocations.
record.test_reason: The report gives MMLU (and other benchmark) scores for three same-family models (3.8B, 7B, 14B) trained on a filtered/synthetic 'data optimal' recipe. It also shows a Figure 3 'scaling law' of log MMLU error against log size. This bears weakly on V6 in a new data setting. No loss, fits or extrapolation are reported, and size is confounded with tokens (3.3T vs 4.8T) and, for phi-3-small, with architecture and tokenizer.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors claim their filtered web plus synthetic data recipe lets small models match much larger ones, deviating from standard scaling laws, which assume a fixed data source. They call the 7B and 14B models significantly more capable than phi-3-mini. They also say some benchmarks improve much less from 7B to 14B, perhaps because the mixture is not 'data optimal' for 14B.
record.recipe_differences: The report uses heavily filtered web data and synthetic data and focuses on data quality; it does not reproduce the original held-out-loss scaling or compute-allocation procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that some benchmark gains differ across size intervals and suggest the data mixture may not be data-optimal for the 14B model.
record.problems: The relevant scaling comparison is sparse; model size and training-token count are not held constant against one another. The paper reports downstream scores rather than held-out pretraining loss, and supplies no uncertainty estimates for these scores. Figure 3's plotted values are not available in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark scores in the academic-benchmark tables are not separately extracted; the reported MMLU comparison and the stated Figure 3 scaling plot are the results most directly tied to size-related downstream performance.

untested.parts: No fits on small runs or extrapolation.
No compute-optimal allocation; authors explicitly train outside the compute-optimal regime.
No shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fits for vision or other regimes; phi-3.5-Vision is only benchmarked.
No fitted trend, no prediction from smaller models or from pretraining loss. Only three sizes, with confounded tokens and architecture.
No exponents or fitting choices compared. Figure 3's claim that the data recipe shifts the curve relative to Llama-2 has no readable values.

missing.what: Other benchmark scores across the three Phi-3 sizes, including non-monotone cases. Read from the jumbled table: ANLI 52.8/58.1/55.8; MATH 41.3/34.6/53.1; TriviaQA 64.0/58.1/73.9; GSM-8K 82.5/89.6/91.0; MT-bench 8.38/8.70/8.91.
Figure 3: log MMLU error vs log model size for phi-1.5, phi-2, phi-3-mini and phi-3-small against the Llama-2 family. Plotted values are not in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a model technical report, not a scaling study. Any V6 evidence is three confounded points with no uncertainty; weight it lightly. The reader's T2 fits poorly; T3 (new data regime) is closer. The phi-3.5 MoE and Vision results are not scaling tests.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small runs predict substantially larger runs.
The compute-optimal parameter and token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss in other modalities or training regimes.
The report gives downstream benchmark results across sizes, but does not test prediction from pretraining loss or establish predictive performance across a broad set of tasks and scales.
It does not estimate loss exponents or compare fitting choices or compute-optimal splits. Its discussion of data quality and scaling is not a test of those specific claims.

rows.subject: phi-3-mini
rows.note: One point in the reported size comparison; training-token count also differs from the larger models.
rows.check: A single point at the smallest size. It serves as the reference for r2/r3 and cannot show a scaling effect alone. The model is chat-finetuned, not a pretrained base.

rows.subject: phi-3-small
rows.note: One point in the reported size comparison; training-token count also differs from phi-3-mini.
rows.check: Baseline should be r1 (68.8): a +6.9 gain from 3.8B to 7B. Confounded: the 7B also has 4.8T vs 3.3T tokens, a different tokenizer, GEGLU, blocksparse attention and 10% extra multilingual data.

rows.subject: phi-3-medium
rows.note: One point in the reported size comparison. The authors also say some benchmarks improve less from 7B to 14B than from 3.8B to 7B.
rows.check: Baseline should be r2 (75.7): only +2.3 for a doubling of size, and authors say some benchmarks improve much less from 7B to 14B. Same token count as r2 but a different architecture from phi-3-small (14B follows the phi-3-mini design).

relationships.reason: MMLU rises from 68.8 to 75.7 with size (r1, r2), though tokens and architecture also change.
relationships.display_finding: MMLU increased from 68.8 to 75.7, although training tokens and architecture also changed.

relationships.condition: Phi-3 7B to 14B on the same 4.8T-token data mixture
relationships.reason: MMLU gains shrink to +2.3 (r3 vs r2). Authors say some benchmarks improve much less, blaming a non-optimal data mixture. Per the text's table, ANLI falls 58.1 to 55.8.
relationships.display_finding: MMLU gained only 2.3 points, while ANLI fell from 58.1 to 55.8, with the authors attributing weak gains on some benchmarks to the data mixture.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Phi-3 MMLU 5-shot results across 3.8B, 7B, and 14B models
reader_labels.reason: MMLU scores rise from 68.8 to 75.7 to 78.0 (r1–r3), but these sparse comparisons do not test prediction, and the training-token count changes between phi-3-mini and the larger models.
